Hi Priya — thanks for sending this over. We've completed Redwood's consolidated answers and attached an evidence manifest and SOC2 summary. A few quick notes inline:

- Detection architecture: We operate a hybrid pipeline: real-time classifiers at the API edge for high-severity patterns (policy-flagging within 100–200ms) plus a downstream batch analysis that recomputes signals with longer context (hourly aggregations).
- Investigator & notification SLAs: For confirmed high-severity customer-impact incidents we aim to acknowledge within 1 hour and provide a triage update within 8 business hours. For lower-severity policy violations (suspected misuse pattern) the standard is 24–48 hours for initial triage. Contractable SLA windows can be scoped in the Dedicated/private offering.
- Telemetry & retention: We log request metadata, actioned policy flags, model variant, token counts, and KV cache traces. Default telemetry retention for hosted tenants is 90 days; Dedicated/Private can extend to customer-specified retention tied to storage and compliance agreements.

I've attached: Redwood_Completed_Questionnaire_v1.pdf, evidence_bundle_manifest.csv, soc2_summary_redwood.pdf.

Vanessa — quick technical clarifications below; copying the language you can lift directly into the questionnaire where helpful.

1) Edge detection latency: 100–200ms is achievable for lightweight policy classifiers and common generation profiles on our hosted fleet; heavier model variants (e.g., long-context >8k and larger decoder-only checkpoints) can push edge decision latency to 250–400ms. We recommend that the questionnaire answer clarify: "Typical edge flagging latency: 100–200ms for standard LLMs and short sequences; up to 400ms for large models or extended contexts."

2) False-positive handling & feedback loop: We maintain a labeled-incident queue where analyst feedback updates model scoring and rule thresholds. Typical FP rate (system-flagged vs human-confirmed) varies by vertical; for generalized web prompts we observe 6–12% FP at our production threshold tuned for precision. We can provide a redacted sample set and a small labelled dataset for ScoutBridge to run verification on — pinged the security lab to prepare a 2k-record sample.

3) Telemetry fields & retention (for the questionnaire): request_id, model_variant, token_count, policy_flag_code, action_taken (block/warn/none), timestamp_utc, region, request_hash (salted). Retention: default 90 days; configurable to 365 days for Dedicated contracts; encrypted-at-rest and role-based access for customer data.

4) Alerts & notification workflow: automated high-severity alerts (policy_flag_code in P0/P1) generate immediate PagerDuty incidents to a monitored SRE roster and send a secure email to the customer's primary security contact. For customers requiring SOC-style notification logs we include a signed digest on request.

Shared drive with supporting docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefGHIjklMnoPqRst
